However, they said that as Earth’s temperature rose due to human activities such as burning oil, gas, and coal, the likelihood of such disasters increased, especially in the Himalayan mountains, which were warming considerably faster than many other parts of the world. #Himalayan #Flood #Nepal #Share #FY

After hearing about the devastating flash floods, we flew to Nepal within 24 hours and immediately began working on getting essential needs and supplies to communities that urgently needed them. With the guidance of a licensed Nepalese doctor, we were able to purchase essential medicines. We then learned about the situation in Rasuwa and how difficult it was for aid to reach the area because of landslides, mud, and constant rain. A 4–6 hour drive turned into more than 24 hours, but we made it to Betrawati and were able to deliver the medicine to the only accessible hospital serving flood victims in the area and nearby districts. Seeing the destruction in Betrawati in person was something I don’t think any of us were prepared for. This was once a community, and seeing what remains of it is heartbreaking. There is still so much work to be done, and we’re staying here for the next few days to help however we can. To everyone who has donated, shared, or supported us in any way, thank you. You are directly helping us get much-needed support to people who need it most.  #nepal #nepalflood

We are already very close to you.” Following the floods, Nepal Army personnel and technical rescue teams have been deployed to search for and rescue people believed to be trapped inside tunnels at various hydropower projects in Rasuwa. Nepal has been hit by a catastrophic flash flood disaster, beginning on 26 August 2026, particularly along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors. 🇳🇵 What happened? The flooding was not simply ordinary monsoon flooding. A sudden ice/rock avalanche and collapse in the Himalayan region near Tibet caused a huge surge of water, mud, rocks and debris into the Bhote Koshi River. The resulting flash flood swept through villages and infrastructure with very little warning.  The worst-affected areas include Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan, with impacts also reported in Gorkha and Tanahun.  🕯️ Deaths and missing people The situation has continued to worsen as rescue teams recover bodies and update missing-person lists. As of 29–30 August, reports indicate more than 600 people have died in Nepal, with thousands still missing across Nepal and Tibet. AP reported 669 deaths in Nepal and nearly 3,000 people still missing as of August 30.  Many of the missing include foreign nationals, tourists, pilgrims and workers. 🚨 Rescue operation Nepalese security forces, helicopters and emergency teams are continuing search-and-rescue operations. More than 3,700 people have reportedly been rescued, while difficult mountain terrain, damaged roads and unstable conditions are making the operation extremely difficult.  A temporary lake formed near the disaster area also created fears of another flood, although the immediate risk has reportedly decreased as the lake has begun draining.  💔 Damage The floods have destroyed or severely damaged: Homes and entire villages Roads and bridges Hydropower plants Electricity infrastructure Border/trade infrastructure Health facilities Tourist and pilgrimage routes Nepal's government estimates that rebuilding could cost approximately US$4–5 billion.  The Nepal Ministry of Foreign Affairs has also been publishing official updates on the disaster and missing foreign nationals.  Important: Some dramatic videos circulating on Sri Lankan social media claiming to show the Nepal floods are actually old or unrelated footage, so they should not automatically be trusted. 🚨 4-Year-Old Child Rescued After 11 Days of Severe Flooding in Nepal Four-year-old Chandrika Shrestha has been rescued from a house in Betravati Bazar, Nuwakot, on the 11th day following severe flooding along the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa, Nepal. The child, from Bidur-10, Nuwakot, was found unconscious during the rescue operation. A command team from the Armed Police Force, Nepal, led by Inspector Suman Bik Shrestha, carried out the rescue. Following the operation, the child was transported by helicopter to the Nepali Army's Maithilac Barracks in Trishuli.
